title: INSTRUCTION CYCLE
summaryPoints: A program is a list of numbered instructions stored as bytes in memory, right next to its data.
Registers are the CPU's tiny, fast storage: PC, MAR, MDR, IR, ACC and the Z flag.
Loading copies the program from disk into memory and points the PC at the first instruction.
Fetch: PC to MAR, read memory into MDR, copy to IR, then add 1 to the PC.
Decode: the opcode picks the action and the operand names the address.
Execute: the ALU, memory or the PC does the work; only this phase differs per instruction.
A jump overwrites the PC, which is how loops and if-statements work.

chapters.name: INTRO
chapters.summary: Every program is a list of tiny steps, and one loop runs them: fetch, decode, execute.

chapters.name: MEMORY
chapters.summary: Memory is numbered boxes of bytes; the same bits can be a number or an instruction, so programs live in memory next to their data.

chapters.name: CPU PARTS
chapters.summary: Registers, the ALU, the control unit and the buses are the parts the cycle moves values between.

chapters.name: LOADING
chapters.summary: The loader copies a program from disk into memory and points the PC at its first instruction.

chapters.name: FETCH
chapters.summary: Fetch copies the next instruction from memory into IR and moves the PC on.

chapters.name: DECODE
chapters.summary: Decode splits the instruction into opcode and operand and lights the right control signal.

chapters.name: EXECUTE
chapters.summary: Execute does the work; it is the only phase that differs between instructions.

chapters.name: FULL RUN
chapters.summary: Running the whole program shows the rhythm: fetch, decode, execute, repeat, until HALT.

chapters.name: JUMPS
chapters.summary: A jump overwrites the PC, and that is how loops and ifs work.

chapters.name: RECAP
chapters.summary: One loop runs every program; real CPUs speed it up by overlapping the phases.
